newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa NUM gets lion's share of Johnnic.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa NUM gets lion's share of Johnnic.

text.p: The National Union of Mineworkers has been allocated the lion's share of the 35 percent stake Anglo American Corp is selling in Johnnic following a National Empowerment Consortium meeting on Thursday.

Local newspapers reported on Friday that the National Empowerment Consortium (NEC) -- a black economic empowerment group comprising labour and business -- had raised more than 2.7 billion rand to pay for the Anglo stake.
Business Day reported that the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) was allocated 12.94 percent of the Anglo stake, effectively a 4.5 percent stake in Johnnic.

The South African Railways and Harbours Union received the second largest allocation of 10.15 percent and union investment vehicle, the Mineworkers' Investment Company, was allocated 3.69 percent of the 35 percent stake.
It reported that a total of 15 unions and union investment companies would be Johnnic shareholders.
Worldwide African Investments, New Africa Investments Ltd and investment company Siphumelele each received 9.82 percent of the total stake.
The three companies' stakes represented an individual investment of about 260 million rand, giving each a 3.4 percent interest in Johnnic.
Consortium splinter grouping, the National Empowerment Corporation, was allocated 8.71 percent, Nozala 6.05 percent, Tswelopele 4.62 percent and Vuyo just under one percent.
